newsitem.title: UK: Blind magistrates to be appointed in Britain.
newsitem.headline: Blind magistrates to be appointed in Britain.

text.p: Britain's top legal officer said on Thursday he hoped to appoint six blind people over the next year to become magistrates, a role they have been denied until now.
The Lord Chancellor, Lord Irving, said in a statement he believed society's attitudes to the disabled had changed in recent years and people were more aware of their abilities.

"I am persuaded that those who are blind from birth, or from their early years, do seem to have an enhanced ability to hear and to draw similar conclusions from their aural sense as those who are lucky enough to be sighted," Irving said.
After the first blind magistrates were appointed he would able to gauge the practical difficulties they encountered and would then decide whether to appoint more.
He made no mention of deaf people, who are still barred from becoming magistrates.
Irving was appointed by the Labour government which swept to power in the May 1 election and has Britain's first blind cabinet minister, Education Secretary David Blunkett.
